results.title: Cut Score: Essential Guide to Test Thresholds & Standard Setting | Cogn-IQ
results.content: # Cut Score. A cut score is a predetermined threshold on a test that divides examinees into different performance categories, typically pass/fail or proficiency levels. Established through systematic standard-setting procedures involving subject matter experts, cut scores transform continuous test scores into categorical decisions for purposes like certification, graduation, or placement. These predetermined thresholds on tests or assessments serve to classify examinees into different performance categories, transforming continuous score distributions into discrete decisions that can profoundly impact individuals' educational and career trajectories. The process of establishing cut scores, known as standard setting, combines psychometric science with professional judgment to determine the minimum level of knowledge, skill, or ability required for a particular classification. Unlike norm-referenced interpretations that compare individuals to each other, cut scores provide criterion-referenced interpretations based on absolute performance standards. The most common application is a single cut score creating a binary classification (pass/fail), though multiple cut scores can establish performance levels such as basic, proficient, and advanced. Cut scores serve to operationalize performance standards, translating abstract expectations into concrete numerical thresholds. Cut scores are fundamentally criterion-referenced, meaning they represent absolute standards of performance rather than relative comparisons. This approach directly links the cut score to external performance criteria but requires valid external classifications. In K-12 education, cut scores determine proficiency levels on state assessments, affecting school accountability ratings and student advancement. Standardized tests like the SAT and ACT often have informal cut scores used by institutions for admissions decisions, though these are typically institution-specific rather than test-publisher determined. Placement tests for developmental education use formal cut scores to determine whether students need remediation in mathematics, reading, or writing before taking college-level courses. * Use multiple standard-setting methods to triangulate appropriate cut scores. Establishing the validity of cut scores requires multiple sources of evidence. Criterion-related evidence examines whether those passing the cut score perform better on external measures than those failing. The standard error of measurement (SEM) around the cut score is particularly critical, as measurement error is greatest near the decision point. Some testing programs implement confidence bands around cut scores or require multiple testing opportunities to reduce misclassification due to measurement error.

results.title: From Pilot to Scale: How to Operationalize AI Across Teams | Raidu - Enterprise AI Governance Platform
results.content: # From Pilot to Scale: How to Operationalize AI Across Teams. # From Pilot to Scale: How to Operationalize AI Across Teams. This article offers practical guidance to help organizations successfully operationalize AI across teams, drawing on my experience as a senior AI strategist. The first step towards operationalizing AI across teams is to build a strong foundation. It’s important to invest in training and development to ensure your team members have the necessary skills to work with AI. In addition to technical training, it’s crucial to build AI literacy across the organization. Data is the lifeblood of AI, but it also presents significant risks. Once your AI systems are operational, it’s crucial to monitor their performance regularly. Regular audits can help to identify any issues and ensure that your AI systems are performing as expected. By building a strong foundation, developing AI skills and literacy, ensuring data governance and compliance, and evaluating and monitoring AI performance, you can successfully scale AI throughout your organization.
